author: nashatyrev
content:

author: barnabemonnot
content: in the worst case attestations go out at 3s, but in happy cases they go out as soon as the block is received. with the proof in the beacon block, the block gets larger, but I wonder if 3s isn't still more generous than needed. is it worth modelling bigger beacon blocks and attestations sent out on receipt of the block?

author: m.kalinin
content: How big bandwidth and computation consumption are expected in the public mempool after switching to PQ signatures comparing to what we have today? If public mempool bandwidth consumption is going to be high then it also need to be considered in p2p simulations, I think

author: derekchiang
content: <@857052906495017000> and i did some benchmarking and at today's TPS (~33 tx/s), assuming all txns become PQ (SPHINCS), the public mempool has no issues propagating the transactions; there's a ton of spare bandwidth right now even for home nodes.  the issue is that blocks become about ~1.9MB in size, so it doesn't always propagate to enough of the network (with or without ePBS).  so we might need some networking optimizations like 8411 to give block propagation more headroom

author: m.kalinin
content:
> there's a ton of spare bandwidth right now even for home nodes.

PQ-Gasper will likely eat out much more bandwidth than it does today. I would like to consider cross-layer bandwidth consumptions for PQ. One of the questions this will help to answer is whether we will have to increase hardware and bandwidth requirements for nodes in the case of PQ-Gasper and PQ-DC

author: derekchiang
content: to be more precise, with my simulation, pre-Glamsterdam the blocks almost never reach enough nodes.  post-Glamsterdam, they reach enough nodes if builders reveal by 1-2s, but not if they reveal at 3s.  so that's what i meant by maybe we need networking optimizations like 8411 to have more headroom
